newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on fund buying.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on fund buying plus seasonal considerations, traders said.
"It was all fund buying, Rosenthal bought one half million (bushels) near the close," a trader said.
Rosenthal Collins also bought 2.5 million bushels early in the session, traders said.
"Seasonally wheat should be going up," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Wheat opened lower. "I think wheat just got dragged down with the beans," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Volume was light as the market sought direction. Traders noted the Columbus Day government holiday caused a void because USDA normally provides export inspection and crop data on Mondays.
News Algeria had issued a snap tender for 100,000 tonnes U.S. and French soft wheat and news Morocco was seeking 40,000 tonnes of wheat contributed to the advances, traders said.
Wheat closed 2-1/4 cents lower to five cents per bushel higher, with December up five at $4.29-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, down from 17,577 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Refco Inc sold 200 March $4.20 puts at 20 cents and Tenco Inc bought 200 December $4.40 calls at 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, down from 5,517 Friday.
